limitations: An idealized vertical throw; real balls feel drag.
title: At the Top of a Vertical Throw
story:
When you toss a ball straight up into the air, it slows down as it rises, momentarily stops at its highest point, and then speeds up as it falls back down. Because the ball's velocity is zero at the very top, it is easy to wonder if its acceleration is also zero for that split second. After all, if something is not moving, how can it be changing its motion? To find out, we can track both the position and the velocity of the ball moment by moment.

Imagine capturing a strobe photograph of the throw. As the ball rises, the distance it covers in each equal time interval gets smaller and smaller until it reaches the apex. At the exact top, the velocity is indeed zero. Yet, if the acceleration were zero there, the ball would simply float or stay suspended at the top instead of turning around. Gravity keeps pulling downward with a steady acceleration even when the velocity vanishes.
cardDescription: Explore what happens to velocity and acceleration at the apex of a vertical throw where $v = 0$ but acceleration remains $-g$.
instructions: Change the launch speed or gravity, then press Play to observe how the tossed ball and the released ball move together.
learningGoal: Explain why the acceleration is not zero at the top, where the velocity is zero, by comparing the tossed ball with a ball released from rest.

scene.description: Two equal-width lanes side by side in one frame: a Toss lane (frame object id lane.toss) and a Drop lane (lane.drop), each with a heading and a state line. Both use the same fixed height scale and the same velocity-arrow and acceleration-arrow scales; zero height is the launch mark, up is positive. A release gate at the apex height holds the second ball (velocity and acceleration zero) until the top, then opens. Each ball (ball.toss, ball.drop) has a blue velocity arrow and a dashed warm acceleration arrow, and a callout (callout.toss, callout.drop) of two readings. After release faint outlines keep the shared starting height. No graph, no mass control, no snapshot strip.

entities.label: Tossed ball
entities.purpose: The ball thrown upward from the launch mark in the Toss lane (frame object id ball.toss).

entities.label: Dropped ball
entities.purpose: The second ball in the Drop lane (frame object id ball.drop), held by the gate until the top.

entities.label: Release gate
entities.purpose: Holds the second ball at the apex height, opens at the top.

entities.label: Velocity arrow
entities.purpose: Blue arrow with the signed velocity of each ball (frame object ids vec.v.toss, vec.v.drop).

entities.label: Acceleration arrow
entities.purpose: Dashed warm arrow with the net acceleration of each ball (frame object ids vec.a.toss, vec.a.drop).

quantities.label: Launch speed
quantities.meaning: Upward speed at the instant of the throw.
quantities.reference: Measured at the launch mark, up is positive.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Magnitude of the constant downward acceleration.

quantities.label: Time of the top
quantities.meaning: Elapsed time from launch at which the velocity is zero.

quantities.label: Height of the top
quantities.meaning: Height of the ball at its top above the ground mark.
quantities.reference: Measured from the ground mark, up is positive.

quantities.label: Toss velocity
quantities.meaning: Signed velocity of the tossed ball, up positive; zero at the top.

quantities.label: Toss acceleration
quantities.meaning: Net acceleration of the tossed ball: -gravity.

quantities.label: Toss height
quantities.meaning: Height of the tossed ball above the ground mark, up positive.
quantities.reference: Measured from the ground mark, up is positive.

quantities.label: Drop velocity
quantities.meaning: Signed velocity of the second ball: zero while the gate holds it, then -gravity * (time from the top). Piecewise at the top.

quantities.label: Drop acceleration
quantities.meaning: Net acceleration of the second ball: zero while the gate holds it, -gravity after the release. Piecewise at the top.

quantities.label: Drop height
quantities.meaning: Height of the second ball: the apex height while the gate holds it, then equal to the tossed ball. Piecewise at the top (switchAt = launchSpeed / gravity).
quantities.reference: Measured from the ground mark, up is positive.

observations.text: The toss velocity changes sign at the top while the acceleration does not.
The toss acceleration stays at -gravity at every instant, including the top.
After the release the dropped ball has the same height, velocity and acceleration as the tossed ball at every shared instant.
A faster toss or a weaker gravity moves the top later and higher; the readings at the top do not change.

checkpoints.label: 0.10 s before the top
checkpoints.expected: The toss velocity is positive and the acceleration is -gravity; the second ball is held, with velocity and acceleration zero.

checkpoints.label: At the top
checkpoints.expected: The toss velocity is zero and its acceleration is still -gravity; the gate opens and the second ball is released at zero velocity.

checkpoints.label: 0.10 s after the top
checkpoints.expected: Both balls move down at the same velocity with acceleration -gravity.

checkpoints.label: Fast toss, weak gravity, at the top
checkpoints.expected: At the fastest toss and the weakest gravity the top comes later and higher; both velocities read zero.

mode.initialState: Launch speed 5 m/s, gravity 9.8 m/s^2; both balls at launch height at the start, time 0.000 s, paused.

controls.label: Play
controls.purpose: Run the motion and replay it.
controls.selectionReason: Time explains the change, and the one supported transport drives every linked view.

controls.label: Time from the top
controls.purpose: Inspect any instant of the motion.
controls.selectionReason: A scrubber lets the learner stop on the instants the explanation compares.

controls.label: Launch speed
controls.purpose: See how the speed of the toss moves the top without changing what gravity does there.
controls.selectionReason: The speed varies continuously and intermediate speeds show that the top moves while the pull does not; two named cases would hide that.

controls.label: Gravity
controls.purpose: See that a different gravity changes the acceleration and the time to the top, not the idea.
controls.selectionReason: Gravity varies continuously and the learner can compare nearby values; two planets would hide that.

controls.label: At top
controls.purpose: Jump to the top of the toss and pause there.
controls.selectionReason: The top is the one instant the explanation is about; a button reaches it exactly, which dragging the scrubber does not.
controls.effect: Seeks the top marker and pauses.

controls.label: Reset experiment
controls.selectionReason: Replay keeps the settings; Reset restores them so the learner can start over.
controls.effect: Restores launch speed 5 m/s, gravity 9.8 m/s^2 and time 0, paused.

claims.text: After the release both balls share height, velocity and acceleration at every instant, and the toss acceleration is -gravity throughout.
claims.check: Toss: y = u t - g t^2 / 2 about its top equals y_top - g tau^2 / 2, the same as a ball released from rest at the top.

assumptions: No air resistance, the same gravity for both balls, up is positive.
